characters.name: Smeden (The Blacksmith)
characters.prompt: A sturdy, middle-aged Norwegian blacksmith from the 1400s-1850s, wearing a soot-stained leather apron, muscular arms from a lifetime of forging metal, a determined face highlighted with ash smudges. He stands by his anvil in a rustic workshop, with a large hammer in hand.

characters.name: Vor Herre (Our Lord)
characters.prompt: A calm, kind-faced figure in simple medieval Norwegian attire, standing with a gentle but wise gaze. He wears a flowing cloak, emanating a soft, comforting glow. His presence feels humble yet divine.

characters.name: St. Peder (Saint Peter)
characters.prompt: A gentle companion to Vor Herre, dressed in plain robes. He has a thoughtful expression and is slightly older in appearance, with a trimmed beard and carrying a staff or walking stick. His manner suggests curiosity and dedicated faith.

characters.name: Fanden (The Devil)
characters.prompt: A cunning figure with a dark, mischievous aura. He appears in subtle demonic form, perhaps with small horns protruding from messy hair, dressed in dark, tattered medieval clothes. He has a sly grin that reveals his trickster nature.

characters.name: Smedens mor (The Blacksmith’s Mother)
characters.prompt: An elderly Norwegian woman of the 1400s-1850s, initially frail and hunched. She has lined features showing her age, dressed in simple rural clothing. Later, she appears rejuvenated as a youthful maiden, wearing a modest but graceful outfit.

cleanedMainImagePrompt: A grand illustration set in rural Norway between 1400 and 1850. The blacksmith’s workshop, with a half-timbered facade, is surrounded by rolling hills under a cloudy sky. A weathered sign above the door reads 'Her bor Mesteren over alle Mestere.' The blacksmith stands confidently by his anvil. Nearby, Vor Herre and St. Peder watch calmly. The Devil lurks to one side, looking both frustrated and cunning. An air of old, mysterious folklore and a hint of humor pervade the scene, capturing the playful yet dramatic tone of the original tale.
modernMainImagePrompt: A contemporary Norwegian setting with a sleek, modern workshop in a small town. The blacksmith, wearing jeans and a well-used welding apron, stands near advanced metalworking tools. The Devil, now sporting a business suit with a mischievous smirk, watches from a corner. Vor Herre and St. Peder appear in simple but modern casual attire, exuding calm and wisdom. There's a sign proclaiming the blacksmith’s mastery, evoking a playful twist on the centuries-old story in a modern context.
childMainImagePrompt: A cheerful, cartoon-like scene set in an old Norwegian village. The friendly blacksmith stands with a big smile at his colorful workshop. Vor Herre and St. Peder look kind and welcoming in simple robes. The Devil is more silly than scary, with small horns and a funny expression. The blacksmith’s mother stands looking happily rejuvenated. Bright colors and gentle shapes create a fun, child-friendly illustration of this folktale.
simplifiedMainImagePrompt: Et norsk landskap i gammel stil, med en enkel smie fra 1400-1850-tallet. Smeden står selvsikkert ved essa si, med et skilt over døra: 'Her bor Mesteren over alle Mestere.' Vor Herre og St. Peder følger med, mens Fanden lurer i bakgrunnen. Bildet viser humoren og den litt magiske stemningen i den gamle folkehistorien.
englishMainImagePrompt: An illustration capturing a traditional Norwegian setting from long ago, with a rustic blacksmith’s forge labeled 'Here Dwells the Master of All Masters.' The sturdy blacksmith stands at the anvil, hammer in hand. Our Lord and Saint Peter, dressed in simple travelers’ robes, observe calmly, while the Devil, slightly hidden in the shadows, looks for a chance to trick the smith. The artwork should reflect the folktale’s blend of humor and supernatural elements, set amid Norway’s rolling hills and timber-built houses.
